## Summary

Fix the subagent activity hook misalignment reported in the Agents and editor windows. The connector was top-aligned and ended 5.5px above the tool icon's center.

- Center the connector relative to the activity row and account for the horizontal stroke's thickness.
- Extend the stem and increase the hook-to-icon gap from 4px to 6px using existing spacing tokens.
- Keep the fix in the shared stylesheet; no DOM, accessibility semantics, or tool behavior changes.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client` — passed, 0 compilation/type errors.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatSubagentContentPart.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed, 154 tests.
- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/media/chatSubagentOpenChat.css` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Live component checks — reproduced the original -5.5px center offset and verified the fix has a 0px offset (within 0.01px) and a 6px gap for five parallel agents, file-read activity in dark/light themes, larger text with a taller activity row, and nested agents in high contrast.
- Existing running-subagent dark/light fixtures — stable across three screenshot samples each; nested high-contrast fixtures — no render/disposal errors.

A captioned before/after MP4 was recorded from live shared production-component fixtures by piping browser viewport frames directly into ffmpeg. The recording uses the original CSS declarations for its baseline, then removes that override to show the compiled fix. Authenticated/live-provider flows were not exercised.

## How to Test

1. Start a chat with active subagents in either the Agents window or the editor window.
2. Check both the initial "Working on it..." row and a subsequent tool activity row.
3. Confirm the hook's horizontal stroke meets the activity icon's centerline and the icon has a little more separation from the hook.
4. Check light/dark/high-contrast themes, nested agents, and zoomed or larger-text layouts.

For deterministic preview, use the existing Component Explorer fixtures `chat/widget/chatWidget/PersistentProgress/ToolChains/ParallelSubagents/Dark`, `chat/chatRendering/SubagentRead/{Dark,Light}`, and `chat/chatSubagentContent/NestedSubagent/DarkHighContrast`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or update the active-tool row for visible running subagents in the Agents or editor chat UI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tool-state changes update the toolbar context and active-tool DOM, after which browser style/layout/paint determines the connector position. The diff adds no JavaScript work and no asynchronous dependency to this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One connector DOM node per visible subagent pill; cost scales with the number of simultaneously visible subagents, but each changed declaration remains constant-time static CSS.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each visible pill is laid out by the browser during the same rendering cycle; the diff introduces no queue, task, timer, IPC, or unbounded parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The shared stylesheet and existing DOM nodes are reused. Cold and warm behavior are unchanged; there are no cache keys, misses, invalidations, or coalescing changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete diff is static CSS, and the owning widget creates one connector node per pill and updates sibling classes/content without reading connector geometry. Existing forced layout for label transition animation is unchanged and independent of these connector declarations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact browser style/layout duration varies with the number of visible subagents and platform, but changing a fixed height, margin, alignment, and transform does not increase DOM cardinality or introduce geometry reads, animation, or repeated script-driven relayout.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The change adjusts constant-size flex layout and a transform on an existing node; it does not add work frequency, retained state, boundary calls, or a synchronous read-after-write cycle.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize, zoom, larger-text, and theme changes while subagent activity rows are visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Browser style recalculation and layout recompute the existing connector's fixed token-based geometry. The percentage transform resolves from the connector's own fixed height and remains declarative; no script waits on this work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of currently rendered subagent pills affected by the shared selector.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser rendering handles all affected elements in its normal frame pipeline; no new listeners, observers, animations, or concurrent tasks are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Theme token resolution and stylesheet reuse are unchanged. The diff neither creates nor bypasses a cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed properties are static layout/transform values on the pre-existing connector, with no changed DOM ownership or event path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frame cost depends on the existing rendered chat size, but the changed properties do not expand the selector scope or add paint-heavy effects; the connector grows by a few pixels only.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Recalculation already occurred for these UI changes before the PR, and the diff does not materially amplify per-element layout or paint complexity.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed CSS hunk and traced the connector through its widget creation and tool-state update paths. Considered synchronous UI work, repeated work, rendering/layout scaling, allocation/retention, cache lifecycle, concurrency, and expensive boundaries. No actionable diff-introduced performance issue or qualifying regression fix was found.
